interest: Illuminates prewar copyright disputes, creative Berne Convention legal strategies, and claims against impounded Japanese assets.
overview: This file documents State Department diplomatic and legal correspondence from 1932 to 1949 regarding intellectual property disputes in Japan, focusing on unauthorized Japanese translations and reproductions of American works. It centers largely on author W. Jefferson Davis’s campaign against the pirated translation of his book on Japanese air power, highlighting novel legal arguments utilizing simultaneous British publication to claim Berne Convention protection and bypass the translation exclusions of the 1905 bilateral treaty. The file also covers diplomatic protests over unauthorized offset reprints of American technical books, an unauthorized movie adaptation of Gone With the Wind, and wartime inquiries concerning compensation from impounded Japanese assets.
